Tool result:
Datasheet gfps-165-solenoid-valve, pages [2, 5, 1, 6, 4]:
This is a Type 165 servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm solenoid valve with a PVC (PVC-U) housing and an epoxy-molded solenoid coil, and yes — it is rated for continuous duty: the datasheet states "Nominal mode of operation: Continuous operation 100 % ED" (ED = "Einschaltdauer", i.e. duty cycle, so 100 % ED means the coil can stay energized permanently) [p. 2]. The valve is also listed with "Mode of operation: A" for all nominal diameters DN15–DN50 in the Kv 100 values table [p. 2].

Details you may need:

- Valve type: servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm valve [p. 1]; needs a minimum differential pressure of 0.5 bar to open and close [p. 1].
- Nominal diameters: DN15 – DN50; housing PVC; gasket EPDM or FKM [p. 2].
- Coil insulation class: Class H [p. 2] (the insulation class indicates how heat-resistant the coil winding is rated).
- Supply voltage: 24 V DC, 230 V 50/60 Hz, 115 V 50/60 Hz, with ±10 % voltage tolerance [p. 2, p. 4].
- Solenoid coil moulding material: chemically highly resistant epoxy [p. 1].
- Replacement coil sets are available for 24 V DC, 230 V AC and 110 V AC with EPDM or FKM gasket — order codes 198 808 029–034 (see the "Coil set (1)" table on page 6) [p. 6].
- Manual override is fitted, described as service-friendly and robust [p. 1].

No specific overheat warning, temperature limit for the coil, or additional duty-cycle conditions are given in the datasheet beyond the "Continuous operation 100 % ED" rating [p. 2].

It can also be specified at ordering via alarm-level option codes: C4 (NAMUR, alarm high), CN (NAMUR, alarm low), CR/CS (custom high/low), CT (Rosemount standard low). Note: the datasheet describes only the jumper/switch method for changing the fail direction; software-menu configuration is not stated. Alarm current levels: default high ≥21.75 mA / low ≤3.75 mA; NAMUR high ≥22.5 mA / low ≤3.6 mA; custom high 20.2–23.0 mA, low 3.6–3.8 mA.

trace.content: Consider the transmitter that feeds controller FIC-11-1. When the transmitter fails, does the output go high or low, and how do I change that alarm direction?

{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "FT-11-1", "question": "What is the fail action / failure mode of this transmitter (fail high or fail low), and is there an option or setting for configuring the alarm/fail direction?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [88, 15, 26, 74, 42, 52, 63, 83]:
**Answer:** The transmitter can fail either high or low — the direction is not fixed, because it is user-selectable. For the HART 4-20 mA output (code A), high or low failure mode is chosen with a jumper/switch on the transmitter [p. 88]; for the low-power output (code M), it is chosen with an internal jumper [p. 88].

**What happens on failure and at what levels:**

- **HART 4-20 mA (output code A):** If self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven either high or low to alert the user [p. 88]. The actual current depends on the configured alarm levels — see Table 5 on page 88:
  - Default setting: high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (for some option codes — M6, DA1, T9, RK — the high alarm default is ≥ 22.5 mA)
  - NAMUR compliant (option codes C4 or CN): high alarm ≥ 22.5 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.6 mA
  - Custom levels: high alarm 20.2–23.0 mA, low alarm 3.6–3.8 mA (with the rule that the low alarm must be 0.1 mA less than low saturation and the high alarm 0.1 mA greater than high saturation)

- **Low-power output (code M):** On a gross transmitter failure the analog signal is driven below 0.94 V (low alarm) or above 5.4 V (high alarm), selected by internal jumper [p. 88].

- **Outputs F, W and X (e.g. Fieldbus, Wireless):** There is no high/low drive; a gross failure is passed as an alert and a status along with the process variable [p. 88].

**Ordering options:** The fail/alarm direction can also be set at ordering via the "alarm levels" option codes for HART 4-20 mA (code A) outputs only: C4 (NAMUR, alarm high), CN (NAMUR, alarm low), CR/CS (custom high/low alarm and saturation levels), CT (Rosemount standard low alarm) — see the ordering tables for 3051C [p. 15], 3051T [p. 26], 3051CFA [p. 42], 3051CFC [p. 52], 3051CFP [p. 63] and 3051L [p. 74].

Note: the factory default configuration is a **high** alarm [p. 109]. I could not find in these facts how to change the fail direction via software menus (only the jumper/switch selection is described).

trace.content: Regarding FT-11-1 on the P&ID: What torque should the coplanar flange bolts be tightened to?
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "FT-11-1", "question": "What torque should the coplanar flange bolts be tightened to?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [113, 8, 93, 99, 96, 88, 109, 72]:
I could not find a torque value for the coplanar flange bolts in this datasheet. The facts cover bolt sizes and materials, but no tightening torque is given anywhere.

What the datasheet does say about these bolts:
- Bolt material options for the coplanar flange/adapters (p. 113, "Bolts for flanges and adapters"): standard is plated carbon steel per ASTM A449, Type 1; option L4 is austenitic 316 SST bolts; option L5 is ASTM A193, Grade B7M bolts; option L6 is alloy K-500 bolts. (SST = stainless steel.)
- Bolt material options with part group "Non-wetted parts" are also listed on p. 93 ("Bolts"): plated carbon steel per ASTM A449 Type 1; austenitic 316 SST per ASTM F593; ASTM A193 Grade B7M alloy steel; alloy K-500.
- The flange bolts themselves are identified as parts in the exploded view, Figure 7 on page 96 (callout for flange bolts).
- For the optional B4 mounting bracket (2-inch pipe or panel), Figure 11 on page 99 shows 5/16-18 bolts (not supplied) and 3/8-16 bolts — but again, no torque is given.

If you need a tightening torque, it is not in this document; you would need to ask the manufacturer or another source (I cannot provide a value beyond these facts).
